A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpatialReasoner-R1, fDPO and M3CTS. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original spatial and general vision-language evaluations, alpha/lambda ablations and qualitative model comparisons in Tables 1–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a qualitative height-estimation failure case in Appendix F and Figure 9.

M1.justification: The segmented fDPO objective, spatial rewards, four M3CTS stages and multimodal inputs/outputs remain unchanged. The newly stated Sa2VA/InternVL2.5 foundation documents the architecture without establishing an architectural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Open Spatial-derived training data, SpatialRGPT-Bench tasks and eight general vision-language benchmarks. The added bedroom example concerns height estimation already represented in the evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all ten external baselines and six SpatialReasoner-R1 variants. Table 2 still compares fDPO 8B against SpatialRGPT-8B, and the retained qualitative comparisons use the same models.

E3.justification: The reported training settings, 4B/8B configurations, 657 qualitative and 749 quantitative evaluation pairs, GPT-4o grading and ±25% numerical tolerance are retained. The added failure example introduces no distinct evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds one height-estimation failure analysis in Appendix F and Figure 9, examining an incorrect furniture-based scale estimate. The alpha/lambda sweeps and previous successful qualitative examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 are unchanged. v2 newly reports a failure in which SpatialReasoner-R1 estimates a dresser mirror's height as 2.0 m against a 1.5 m reference; the earlier qualitative examples are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–11 for preference optimization, rewards and tree search remain equivalent. No substantive assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The principal contributions and state-of-the-art claims remain. However, v2 newly characterizes the headline 4.1% and 9.0% gains as relative gains. Table 1 instead implies 4.11 and 9.08 percentage-point differences, making this a limited but inaccurate recasting of the quantitative claim.

C2.justification: v2 attributes the new height-estimation failure to overreliance on typical furniture dimensions and discusses checking image-derived geometry and intermediate reasoning. The existing limitations concerning explicit region inputs and extension beyond 2D reasoning remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly identifies Sa2VA, based on InternVL2.5, as the model foundation. The disclosed optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes, H100 hardware, training time, data construction, reward prompt and project access information otherwise remain equivalent.

R1.justification: v2 adds Shikra, CALICO, PRIMA and Ranasinghe et al.'s object-localization work, while removing Li, Hogg and Cohn's spatial-reasoning simulation benchmark citation. The central positioning remains similar; publication-metadata updates and relocation of related work do not constitute additional research coverage.

P1.justification: The detailed related work moves from v1 Appendix A into a condensed Section 2, replacing the short main-text summary. Other prose edits are localized, with added acknowledgments and author/header updates; most scientific prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adopts NeurIPS typography, margins and page layout throughout. It redraws and separates the combined overview into training and architecture Figures 1–2, revises teaser annotations, resizes and relocates retained displays, and adds failure Figure 9. This is a substantial visual reorganization.

improvement.justification: The concrete failure analysis and explicit Sa2VA/InternVL2.5 attribution modestly improve transparency and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the localized reporting regression introduced by calling percentage-point differences relative gains. The principal experimental and mathematical evidence remains unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
